warnings: The model starts at 08:00 (START CLOCKTIME), so its hour 0 is 08:00, not midnight. When this file is uploaded to the app (or run with the pilot's --inp), the app and the pilot convert (task 16): a grab log's times of day become model hours (the time minus 8 h, mod 24 h), and the app shows the route's hours, the worst hour, the hour picker and each junction's hour of the daily minimum as times of day. Hours typed into the app's sample table stay model hours: take 8 h off a sample's time of day before typing it. Add 8 h to a model hour for the time of day.
3 patterns longer than a day and not a week (1: 55 h, 2: 55 h, 3: 55 h): EPANET repeats each one over its own length, so the scored day (the last of the 7-day run) is not a repeat of one daily cycle.
The file's own source at 1 is overridden: the tool doses every entry point with the dose you set.

fixes: Set the reaction order to 1, as the decay model assumes (first order), where the file had bulk 0.0 and tank 0.0 and wall 0. An order of 0 is another law (a fixed amount lost per day), so the decay rates would not mean what they say, and the bulk rate can have no effect at all.
warnings: 3 junctions at elevation 0 in a model with pressure-control valves: JUNCTION-3215, JUNCTION-3216, JUNCTION-3322. If a 0 means 'not surveyed', the pressure there is wrong, and near a valve or a pressure-based control so are the flows. In a test on the public model ky10 (its 5 PRVs), setting every junction to one elevation moved the water age by more than 2 h at 90 of 920 junctions, by up to 47.4 h (outputs/intake/elevation_prv_ky10.json). Check these elevations in the modelling package.

Pumps but no controls: 1 of 61 pumps has no control, rule or speed pattern (open all the time: PUMP-3889), so it stays as the file starts it for all 7 days. If the real pumps cycle, the water age and the tanks' chlorine are wrong: export the model with its controls.

Large model: 3323 junctions, more than 3000. The grid is 675 runs and a file of about 215.3 MB (the run cost row has the time), so building it needs an explicit confirm (a checkbox in the app's readiness report, or --allow-large in the pilot). The model is not skeletonized: trimming branches would delete the dead ends, where residuals are lowest.
